title: Work that predates the call is changed only on a named instruction; ambiguity gets a question

dayLine.title: Follow up with Dana at The Louise

turns: Tomorrow I've got the Century Park East delivery in the morning. And the Wilshire Vermont walk-in after lunch.
The Louise? I didn't say anything about the Louise. That's not something I need to think about right now.
No, leave it. But take the Opus pickup off tomorrow, they rescheduled. And the Chadwick pitch is done, I did it this afternoon.

notes: Guards the principle 'proactive about new work, conservative about old work'. Turn 1 is dictation of two new items: both written, no ask. Turn 3 names a pre-existing item (the Louise follow-up) and instructs nothing: it must stay; the right move is to say it was already on the list and ask once whether to take it off (that is the one allowed ask). Turn 4 answers 'leave it' and gives two explicit, named instructions about pre-existing work: the Opus pickup comes off tomorrow (removal, not abandonment), the Chadwick pitch is marked completed. The license row three days out is never mentioned and must be untouched.
